scope: Corollary 1.2 (Length cutoffs) of the manuscript “Radial transfer estimates and polygon length laws for honeycomb walks” (preprints/Radial-transfer-estimates-and-polygon-length-laws-for-honeycomb-walks-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 02d2e8df0dcf370b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The length tails satisfy X L(γ)≥n w(γ) = n−3/2+o(1) , X L(γ)≥n L(γ)w(γ) = n−1/2+o(1) . Under either normalized weight w(γ) or L(γ)w(γ), conditioned on L(γ) ≥ n, one has D(γ) = n3/4+o(1) in probability. The same conclusion holds with the length restriction n ≤ L(γ) < n1+δ for any fixed δ > 0. Under the length-weighted law conditioned on D(γ) ≥ r, one has L(γ) = r4/3+o(1) in probability. An assertion Xt = ta+o(1) in probability means that its value lies between ta−ε and ta+ε with probability tending to one for every ε > 0.
